subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The gravitational field strength on the surface of the Moon is approximately
options: about one-sixth of that on Earth
exactly the same as that on Earth
about six times that on Earth
zero because the Moon has no atmosphere
questions.explain: The Moon's gravitational field strength is about 1.6 N/kg, roughly one-sixth of Earth's value of about 10 N/kg.

questions.q: Which type of force keeps the planets in orbit around the Sun?
questions.explain: The Sun's gravitational force provides the centripetal force that keeps the planets in orbit.

questions.q: Which equation gives the orbital speed of a body moving in a circular orbit?
questions.explain: Orbital speed equals the circumference of the orbit (2πr) divided by the time period T for one orbit.

questions.q: Which statement correctly compares the orbits of comets and planets?
options: A comet has a highly elliptical orbit, whereas a planet's orbit is almost circular
A comet has a circular orbit, whereas a planet's orbit is highly elliptical
Both comets and planets have perfectly circular orbits
Both comets and planets follow straight-line paths around the Sun
questions.explain: Comets travel on very elongated (elliptical) orbits, while planets follow orbits that are close to circular.

questions.q: A satellite orbits at a radius of 7.0 × 10⁶ m with a time period of 6000 s. What is its orbital speed?
A planet orbits at a radius of 6.0 × 10¹¹ m with an orbital speed of 1.5 × 10⁴ m/s. What is its time period?
questions.explain: Rearranging v = 2πr / T gives T = 2πr / v = 2π × 6.0 × 10¹¹ / 1.5 × 10⁴ ≈ 2.5 × 10⁸ s.

questions.q: The Earth orbits the Sun at a radius of 1.5 × 10¹¹ m with a period of 3.15 × 10⁷ s. What is its orbital speed?
A body has an orbital speed of 2.0 × 10⁴ m/s and a time period of 1.0 × 10⁸ s. What is the radius of its orbit?
questions.explain: Rearranging v = 2πr / T gives r = vT / 2π = 2.0 × 10⁴ × 1.0 × 10⁸ / 2π ≈ 3.2 × 10¹¹ m.

questions.q: Which colour indicates the hottest star?
questions.explain: Star colour is linked to surface temperature: blue stars are the hottest and red stars the coolest.

questions.q: Which sequence shows the life cycle of a star with a mass similar to the Sun?
options: nebula → main sequence star → red giant → white dwarf
nebula → red supergiant → supernova → black hole
main sequence star → red giant → neutron star → nebula
nebula → white dwarf → red giant → main sequence star
questions.explain: A Sun-like star forms from a nebula, becomes a main sequence star, swells into a red giant, and finally becomes a white dwarf.

questions.q: A star much more massive than the Sun may end its life as a
questions.explain: After a supernova, a very massive star leaves behind a neutron star or, if massive enough, a black hole.

questions.q: After the red giant stage, a star with a mass similar to the Sun becomes a
questions.explain: Sun-like stars shed their outer layers after the red giant phase, leaving a hot, dense white dwarf core.

questions.q: The luminosity of a star depends on its
questions.explain: A star's luminosity (power output) increases with both its surface temperature and its size.

questions.q: Before exploding as a supernova, a very massive star becomes a
questions.explain: Very massive stars expand into red supergiants before undergoing a supernova explosion.

questions.q: Compared with a blue star, a red star is likely to be
questions.explain: Redder stars have lower surface temperatures, so a red star is cooler than a blue star.

questions.q: Red-shift is the observation that light from distant galaxies has a
questions.explain: Red-shift means the observed wavelength is longer (shifted towards the red end of the spectrum) than when the light was emitted.

questions.q: The red-shift of distant galaxies provides evidence for which theory?
questions.explain: Red-shift shows galaxies are moving apart, supporting the Big Bang theory that the universe began from a single point and has been expanding.

questions.q: Observations show that more distant galaxies have
options: greater red-shifts, showing they are moving away faster
smaller red-shifts, showing they are moving away more slowly
blue-shifts, showing they are moving towards us
questions.explain: The more distant a galaxy, the greater its red-shift, indicating that it is receding from us more quickly.

questions.q: The red-shift of galaxies is evidence that the universe is
options: getting colder at its centre only
questions.explain: Because almost all galaxies are red-shifted and moving away from us, the universe as a whole must be expanding.

questions.q: The cosmic microwave background (CMB) radiation is regarded as evidence that
options: the universe began with a Big Bang
stars are made mainly of iron
the Earth is at the centre of the universe
questions.explain: The CMB radiation, detected across the whole sky, is the cooled remnant of the hot early universe, strongly supporting the Big Bang theory.
